name: Château de Versailles
known: The Salon de Diane in the King's State Apartment reopened in June 2026 after 18 months of conservation works (stated by the space).
An American Friends of Versailles gala with Becca Cason Thrash as honorary chair raised 3.5 million dollars for the restoration (PaperCity, July 2026).

name: Musée de Tahiti et des Îles – Te Fare Iamanaha
Center of Contemporary Art Tbilisi (Tbilisi Triennial)
known: Independent non-profit contemporary art centre in Tbilisi, founded by the artist and art educator Wato Tsereteli.
The 1st edition, "Offside Effect", was in 2012, curated by Henk Slager and Tsereteli.

name: Georgian National Museum
known: In 2022 he chaired its Directorate, whose other members were appointees of the culture minister (Civil.ge).
It has a conservation laboratory at the Simon Janashia Museum and an auditorium, both set up with BP Georgia's support (BP volume, 2010).

BP and its partners paid for the Rescue Archaeology Programme on the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan and South Caucasus pipelines in 2000 to 2005, and for the full cycle of survey, excavation, conservation, storage, exhibition and publication (BP volume, 2010).

name: Kropka (Belarusian community space; listed in place of 'Krokva')
Kunsthalle Tbilisi
known: Non-profit contemporary art initiative in Tbilisi without a permanent building, led by the curators Irena Popiashvili and Lika Chkuaseli (The Art Newspaper, 16 May 2018).
Its own site describes it as a roving exhibition space founded by the two curators, showing Georgian and international art in locations across Tbilisi (archived February 2023).
Its archived site has one About paragraph naming two founders.

name: Tbilisi Photography & Multimedia Museum (TPMM)
known: Nestan Nijaradze co-founded the non-profit in 2017 with a group of women professionals (Freunde von Freunden, Ann-Christin Schubert, undated).

name: Julia Stoschek Foundation (Julia Stoschek Collection / JSC Berlin)
known: W Magazine (Diane Solway, 20 November 2017) says Stoschek is "an active shareholder" in her family's auto-parts company Brose, whose chairman is her father Michael Stoschek.
Autonomous non-profit foundation gGmbH with transparent public reporting and curatorial independence.

name: KW Institute for Contemporary Art
known: Emma Enderby has been director since May 2024 (the space's about page).

name: Künstlerhaus Bethanien
known: Bethanien names its partners and funders on one undated page but posts no annual reports, accounts or board; its team page names two directors.
